title: "Behavioural Experiment Planner"
description: "Try a small, reasonably safe action to learn about a specific prediction."

Choose an everyday, low-risk question. Do not use experiments to test physical danger, stop treatment, or violate boundaries. A result that supports a concern can guide problem solving or support.

::: {#behavioural-experiment-app .skill-app data-practice-app="behavioural-experiment"}
Loading Behavioural Experiment Planner...
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="A worked example"}
Alex predicts that asking for clarification will annoy a colleague. They ask one clear question during an agreed check-in and note the actual reply. One brief answer may be ambiguous; it is information, not a verdict on Alex's worth.
:::

Keep a [Core Belief Evidence Log](/tool-finder/core-belief-evidence-log/) if you want to compare an experiment with other observations over time.
